micro_flaws.macro_topic: 5. Related work & Citations - Missing Relevant Citations
micro_flaws.core_summary: The paper omits several relevant recent works on multi-turn reinforcement learning and user-simulators for LLMs.

raw_arguments.Human_1: Some related work not included in the paper: 1. Abdulhai, Marwa, et al. "Lmrl gym: Benchmarks for multi-turn reinforcement learning with language models." arXiv preprint arXiv:2311.18232 (2023). 2. Shani, Lior, et al. "Multi-turn reinforcement learning from preference human feedback." arXiv preprint arXiv:2405.14655 (2024).
raw_arguments.Human_5: Would be nice to have a comparison with other works that make use of user-simulators to improve LLMs, such as Zero-Shot Goal-Directed Dialogue via RL on Imagined Conversations (https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.05584).

micro_flaws.macro_topic: 5. Related work & Citations - Missing Comparisons with Prior Work
micro_flaws.core_summary: The paper lacks systematic, quantitative comparisons with prior multi-turn training methods and methods using user simulators, which would better contextualize its contributions.

raw_arguments.Human_5: It would be nice to add discussions explaining the difference of this paper from other prior literature that uses LLMs as user simulators, e.g. ttps://arxiv.org/abs/2311.05584.

micro_flaws.core_summary: The generalization evaluation is limited to only one external dataset (Abg-CoQA), which is insufficient to robustly validate claims of broad generalizability.

raw_arguments.Human_1: Generalization tests were limited to a single additional dataset. Including multiple diverse external benchmarks could strengthen claims about generalizability.

micro_flaws.macro_topic: 3. Applicability, Scalability & Limitations - Scalability & Complexity Concerns
micro_flaws.core_summary: The computational overhead and scalability of the forward-sampling strategy, especially for longer conversations, are not adequately discussed or analyzed.

raw_arguments.Human_1: The paper could benefit from a more detailed discussion of the computational overhead associated with the proposed methods, particularly regarding the scalability of Multiturn-aware Rewards.
raw_arguments.Human_3: Any idea on the computational expensive aspect of the forward sampling strategy? This seems nontrivial especially for long conversations.

micro_flaws.macro_topic: 6. Methodology & Theoretical Soundness - Lack of Intuition/Justification
micro_flaws.core_summary: The causal-effect estimation claim and the distinction between the proposed method and standard self-training with simulated users are unclear and need better justification.

raw_arguments.Human_2: The motivation and design principle behind the methodology must be better conveyed to showcase that this work goes beyond simply engineering and re-designing the self-training framework...

micro_flaws.macro_topic: 7. Reproducibility & Open Science - Insufficient Implementation Details
micro_flaws.core_summary: The paper lacks sufficient implementation details on key parameters, algorithms, and the MR mechanism, hindering reproducibility.

raw_arguments.LLM_Reviewer: Further details on the implementation of the MR mechanism, including the reinforcement learning algorithms used and the exact parameters of the LLM judges, would enhance the reproducibility of the study.

micro_flaws.macro_topic: 7. Reproducibility & Open Science - Missing Code/Data Repository
micro_flaws.core_summary: The proposed new datasets for multi-turn evaluation are not provided or linked in supplementary materials, making their quality and quantity difficult to assess.

raw_arguments.Human_2: Please correct me if I am wrong, but I could not find supplementary materials or anonymized links to these datasets. While the authors provide samples in the Appendix, I would have preferred to see the full datasets to get a clearer picture of the dataset quality and quantity.

micro_flaws.macro_topic: 4. Experimental Design & Evaluation - Insufficient Experimental Validation
micro_flaws.core_summary: The performance gains over prompt-engineered baselines are small (e.g., 35% to 36-38% BLEU), raising questions about the method's real-world impact and validation against stronger baselines like GPT-4o.

raw_arguments.Human_4: The improvements on simulated experiments of tab 1 (35% to 36-38% BLEU, 12.5 to 15) are small between prompt engineering and the proposed method (using PPO or DPO), raising doubts about real impact. With overall small performance improvement and a model size ≤8B parameters, the validation of the method is not 100% convincing to me. What would be the topline obtained w/ gpt4-o and the same prompt engineering for instance ?

micro_flaws.macro_topic: 4. Experimental Design & Evaluation - Questionable Evaluation Metrics
micro_flaws.core_summary: The use of BLEU for the document editing task and the methodology for LLM-based interactivity scoring are questionable and lack sufficient justification or clarity.

raw_arguments.Human_4: Interactivity (ITR): engagement is evaluated using an LLM judge (Claude-3.5-Sonnet) with scores rescaled to [0,1] But how exactly is this scoring performed? The methodology needs more clarity.

micro_flaws.core_summary: The paper assumes the simulated user (a prompted LLM) accurately reflects real human behavior, but does not adequately discuss or validate this assumption, which could limit applicability.

raw_arguments.Human_3: A comparison of the potential divergence of simulated user and human user during training would further strengthen this work, as prompt-defined simulated LLM users could be substantially biased.
raw_arguments.Human_5: It would helpful if the authors can provide some insight in terms of the limitations of applying LLMs as user simulators. In my experience, I found instruction-tuned LLM as user simulators tend to be overly agreeable and always consent to the requests while real users can be harder to deal with.

micro_flaws.macro_topic: 3. Applicability, Scalability & Limitations - Lack of Discussion on Limitations
micro_flaws.core_summary: The paper lacks a dedicated discussion section, limiting the contextualization of results and a thorough analysis of the framework's broader impact and limitations.

raw_arguments.LLM_Reviewer: Additionally, the absence of a discussion section limits the contextualization of results and the reinforcement of the paper's broader impact.

micro_flaws.core_summary: The paper does not clearly articulate its novel contributions in a dedicated section, which may obscure the significance of its innovations.

raw_arguments.LLM_Reviewer: The paper lacks a dedicated section to clearly articulate its novel contributions, which may obscure the significance of its innovations for readers.

micro_flaws.core_summary: The paper contains typographical errors, such as in figure captions.

raw_arguments.Human_4: Typo: -caption of fig 2: Figure 2: Real examples from COLLABLLM and non-collaborative LLM fine-tuing => fine-tuNing

micro_flaws.macro_topic: 4. Experimental Design & Evaluation - Other Evaluation Issues
micro_flaws.core_summary: An observed counter-intuitive result (ITR performance decreasing with a larger sampling window) is not explained, raising questions about the method's understanding.

raw_arguments.Human_4: Figure 4: why does ITR performance decrease when the forward sampling window size increases from w=2 to w=3? This behaviour seems counterintuitive to me. What could explain it?
